source_text: Countries with predominantly non-circumcising populations in East and Southern Africa reported HIV prevalences exceeding 10-20% in urban adults by the early 1990s, compared to under 2-5% in circumcising Muslim-majority nations in West Africa, despite similar sexual network structures.
